To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have shown that the Fanconi anema pathway is differentially affected in BALB/c mice with a high susceptibility to mammary tumors versus C57BL mice with a low susceptibility to mammary cancer.
we have shown that BALB/c-Trps3+/- mice display a functional defect in the Fanconi Anemia (FA) pathway, which is associated with a higher incidence of mammary tumors.
we have discovered a novel modifier allele in the Fanconi pathway, which promotes mammary carcinogenesis of BALB/c-Tr53+/- mice in the context of a partial loss of p53 function.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of breast cancer susceptibility in the context of a mouse model of Li-Fraumenis syndrome.
the identification of genetic factors that contribute to the susceptibility to breast cancer in BALB/c mice and their potential role in human disease.
the identification of a novel BRCA modifier gene in the FA pathway that may be relevant to breast cancer in humans.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a genetic modifier in the FA pathway is responsible for the susceptibility to mammary cancer in BALB/c mice.
BALB/c mice have a BRCA modifier in the FA pathway.

BALB/c-Trpf53+/- mice have a BRCA2 modifier allele in the context of a partial p53 loss of function, which may explain why they are more prone to breast cancer than C57BL/ 6J-Trpf53+/. The study also demonstrates the power of a siRNA screening approach to identify functional differences in DSB repair between two mouse strains.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a BRCA modifier is a critical factor in the etiology and progression of spontaneous mammary cancer in BALB/c mice.
BALB/c-Trps53+/- female mouse mammary carcinogenesis is promoted by an allele that is a modifier of BRCA2, which in turn may act through the FA pathway.
BALB/c-Tr53+/- mice display a BRCA modifier that is likely to be a FA pathway defect.
The main takeaway from our work is that

we have uncovered the genetic basis of a novel mouse model for breast cancer that is characterized by a BRCA2 defect and that can be used to study breast cancer susceptibility in the context of p53 haploinsufficiency.
the genetic background can influence cancer predisposition by affecting the function of genes in DNA repair pathways.
we have identified a new mouse model of breast cancer, which is a good model for the Li-Fraumenis Syndrome and that this mouse model can be used to study the etiology of breast cancer.
